title: Evidence Status and Reading Guide
paragraphs: Evidence Status and Reading Guide This version is a self-contained research archive. It contains the raw 60-row questionnaire le and the reconstructed 52-row analysis matrix, the raw ride/PO narratives, the original 160-segment FGD transcript, the 27.7-minute self-report audio and its 185-segment GPU transcript, the four qualitative corpora, the stimulus metadata, the nal Python pipeline, the R reproduction scripts, the seeds, the generated JSON/CSV outputs, and the thesis gures. The historical two-arm simulation is reported as an inherited model summary; the nal calibrated in-silico experiment (v8.0) is reproduced by the included pipeline and is reported separately. The distinction between measured eld evidence, model-based counterfactual evidence, and theoretical propositions is maintained throughout. Appendix K gives the exact commands, and Appendix L identies the package contents. The questionnaire concerns audience evaluations in a convenience sample. Historical simulation contrasts concern a specied model. The prospective agent experiment concerns computational task performance. These three units of evidence cannot be substituted for one another. The original focus-group transcript is integrated in Appendix G and Section 6.7; the audiovisual recordings and participant roster remain unavailable. The supplemental seven-part generated analysis is available for critical review but is not a substitute for those records (Appendix G.4). The FGD supplies provisional design hypotheses, not additional questionnaire responses. The researcher self-report is included as reexive context; independently xxxvi

LIST OF FIGURES xxxvii keyed factual assessment remains a separate requirement. Chapter 1 introduces the question and evidence streams; Chapter 2 reviews the literature; Chapter 3 develops the proposed framework; Chapter 4 distinguishes platform specications from implementation evidence; Chapter 5 explains the methods and uncertainty; Chapter 6 separates reported ndings from prospective tests; and Chapter 7 states the bounded conclusions. For a short examination path, read the abstract, Section 1.2.3 on why the case is radio-specic, Table 6.26 with Section 6.12.15, Table 6.27 with Section 6.12.17, the trade-o in Section 6.12.6, and the bounded conclusions in Chapter 7. The deep Chapter 6 subsections are kept in place so that the numeric and denitional links remain adjacent. PB and stars Students' evaluations of a broadcast, not demonstrated literacy. Questionnaire BRS Eleven audience-rating items, not the platform's computed reputation score. Algorithmic BRS A proposed platform score whose implementation and calibration need separate checks. Student Rating A distinct proposed competence prole; no eld treatment eect is reported. Uncertainty Condence intervals, posterior credible intervals, and ranges across simulation
